title: D-One Descriptor Vocabulary
description: Contract sketch for the V1/V2 approved descriptor vocabulary named in references/d-one-live-run-readiness.md and references/d-one-live-prerequisites.md. NOT wired into runtime today: no script reads this file at prompt-assembly time, no prompt assembler exists, and there has never been a real D-One call. The schema ships only so references/d-one-live-prerequisites.md can point at concrete field names. V3 closed-enumeration: a runtime prompt assembler, when one is written, MUST refuse any descriptor not present in this file; the live runner MUST re-check this at its own boundary (defense in depth). V2 abstract-only: every entry is one of four kinds — a design-system color token referenced by name, a geometric noun, a mood adjective, or a composition adjective. Proper nouns, product names, customer names, quoted source text, source-derived sentences, dates, and numbers pulled from the source body are forbidden; the schema enforces lowercase-identifier shape via a positive-whitelist 'pattern' lock on every descriptor value (refusing uppercase letters, whitespace, URI schemes, paths, emails, and fragment / query / percent-encoded shapes) AND a negative-lookahead deny clause that refuses forbidden-token shapes at the schema layer — bounded tokens 'public', 'upload', 'raw', 'customer', 'confidential', 'screenshot', 'credential', 'password', 'secret' (matched as standalone identifier tokens with start-of-string / end-of-string / an identifier-boundary char '.' / '_' / '-' on each side, so legitimate words like 'drawing' that merely contain 'raw' mid-word still pass, AND so hyphen-separator forms like 'public-upload' / 'raw-source' / 'customer-acme' / 'confidential-report' and dotted forms like 'public.upload' fail too) and the compound phrases 'full slide', 'image search', 'web generation', 'page generation', 'slide generation' — each compound matched across ZERO OR MORE identifier-boundary chars so the underscore form ('full_slide'), the hyphen form ('full-slide'), the dotted form ('full.slide'), the concatenated form ('fullslide'), AND every separator-stacked obfuscation (multi-char runs like 'full__slide' / 'full--slide' / 'full..slide' / 'full___slide' / 'full----slide', and mixed-separator runs like 'full_-slide' / 'full.-slide' / 'full_.slide') all fail. The deny is a fail-closed schema-layer precaution; the V4 post-assembly re-scan (the adapter's full deny list re-running on every assembled prompt before the plan is written) remains the adapter runtime's responsibility and is still TODO.

schema_version.description: File-shape schema version. Locked to integer 1 today; bumped only with a paired schema/validator change so a future consumer can refuse a shape it does not recognize.

note.description: Self-describing sentinel. MUST contain the literal 'D-One descriptor vocabulary' verbatim so the file is identifiable even when read out of context. Surrounding text is locked to ASCII letters, digits, spaces, and basic sentence punctuation only — refuses URI schemes (no ':'), paths (no '/' or '\\'), emails (no '@'), and fragment / query / percent-encoded shapes (no '#' / '?' / '%').

kind_enum.description: The closed set of descriptor kinds (V2). The array is fixed-length so a tampered file cannot silently widen the vocabulary surface. The runtime gate, when it exists, will cross-check every descriptors[*].kind against this list AND against the same hard-coded enum (defense in depth).

kind.description: One of the four V2 kinds: 'color_token' (design-system palette token referenced by name, never a hex literal pulled from a customer palette), 'geometric_noun' (e.g. circle, wedge, isometric stack), 'mood_adjective' (e.g. calm, energetic, minimal), 'composition_adjective' (e.g. centered, off-axis, balanced).

value.description: Lowercase identifier-shaped descriptor with a forbidden-token deny clause. The positive whitelist refuses uppercase letters (so proper nouns cannot pass), whitespace (so multi-word phrases cannot pass), URI schemes (no ':'), paths (no '/' or '\\'), emails (no '@'), fragment / query / percent-encoded shapes (no '#' / '?' / '%'), and the leading character must be a lowercase letter so '.internal' / '-flag' / '0num' cannot pass. The leading negative lookaheads additionally refuse forbidden-token shapes: bounded tokens 'public', 'upload', 'raw', 'customer', 'confidential', 'screenshot', 'credential', 'password', 'secret' (each matched only when surrounded by start-of-string / end-of-string / an identifier-boundary char '.' / '_' / '-', so 'drawing' and 'palette.background' still pass while 'raw_source', 'raw-source', 'customer_acme', 'customer-acme', 'confidential_report', 'confidential-report', 'public_upload', 'public-upload' all fail), and the compound phrases 'full slide', 'image search', 'web generation', 'page generation', 'slide generation' (each matched across ZERO OR MORE identifier-boundary chars so the underscore form 'full_slide', the hyphen form 'full-slide', the dotted form 'full.slide', the concatenated form 'fullslide', AND every separator-stacked obfuscation — multi-char runs like 'full__slide' / 'full--slide' / 'full..slide' / 'full___slide' / 'full----slide', mixed-separator runs like 'full_-slide' / 'full.-slide' / 'full_.slide', and the same families for the other four compounds — all fail; same for the other four). For 'color_token' entries, the runtime vocabulary validator (when written) MUST cross-check that the value resolves to a 'palette.<name>' token in design_system.json; the schema records the lowercase-identifier shape constraint AND the schema-layer deny against the listed forbidden tokens — the V4 post-assembly adapter re-scan (full deny list against the assembled prompt) remains the runtime's responsibility and is still TODO.

approved_in_review_ref.description: Optional. Opaque reference to the recorded V1 vocabulary approval review under which this descriptor was added. NEVER a real reviewer name, NEVER an email, NEVER any PII shape: the pattern lock refuses '/', '\\', ':', '@', '#'.

descriptors.description: Approved descriptor list. V3 closed-enumeration: an empty array is equivalent to 'no prompt is assemblable' and is the resting state today. V5 paired-change rule: adding, removing, or modifying a descriptor requires a paired update to this file and to the runtime validator (or, if no validator yet exists, the corresponding TODO in references/d-one-live-integration-design.md §13 is still open and the live path stays unwired). V4 post-assembly re-scan: any prompt assembled from these descriptors MUST re-pass the full adapter deny list (URI schemes, file paths, raw-source markers, 40-char source shingles, credential / PII shapes, full-slide / page-generation / screenshot wording) AFTER assembly, BEFORE the plan is written; that gate is the adapter's runtime responsibility, not this schema's.

allowed_values.description: Closed enumeration of permitted rendering-style values. Defense in depth: the items[].enum locks the canonical five tokens, and the items[].pattern re-applies the descriptor-layer positive whitelist + forbidden-token deny clause so a future schema-edit that loosened the enum would still trip the pattern on any unsafe token. Length is pinned to exactly 5 so a tampered file cannot widen the surface; adding or removing a value is a paired schema/template/validator change.

rendering_style.description: Dimension 1 — visual rendering treatment requested for a synthetic image. The five values are clean-room engineering tokens, not a quote of any external rendering-style catalog.

allowed_values.description: Closed enumeration of permitted palette-family values. Each value names HOW the runtime should pull colors from the design-system palette tokens (which are themselves a separate closed contract in design_system.json) — never a raw hex literal pulled from a customer palette.

palette_family.description: Dimension 2 — palette mapping strategy. Each value resolves at runtime against design_system.json's palette tokens; the schema only fixes the strategy enumeration.

allowed_values.description: Closed enumeration of slide-purpose roles a synthetic image is allowed to play. 'full_slide' / 'whole_slide' / 'screenshot' shapes would trip the descriptor deny pattern at the schema layer; only small motif / icon / emblem / divider / cover roles are permitted, matching references/d-one-image-policy.md (the local pipeline never asks D-One for a full slide).

image_role.description: Dimension 3 — slide-purpose role. The role narrows WHAT a synthetic image is for; it never includes any 'full slide' / 'whole page' / 'screenshot' value, which would also be refused by the descriptor pattern itself.

allowed_values.description: Closed enumeration of spatial composition patterns. Each value names a coarse subject placement on the canvas; finer placement is the slide-plan / render-model layer's responsibility, not this taxonomy's.

layout_pattern.description: Dimension 4 — spatial composition pattern. Coarse subject placement only; the slide-plan layout engine still positions the rendered asset on the slide.

allowed_values.description: Closed enumeration of optional intensity / texture modifiers. Each value softens or constrains the rendered output (lower contrast, softer edges, grid-aligned subject, generous negative space).

modifier.description: Dimension 5 — optional intensity / texture modifier. Applied on top of the four required dimensions; never carries product-specific or customer-specific tokens.

image_taxonomy.description: Image-request taxonomy. A synthetic image request is composed from five clean-room dimensions: rendering_style, palette_family, image_role, layout_pattern, modifier. Each dimension declares a fixed-length 'allowed_values' array whose entries are simultaneously enum-locked AND pattern-locked at the schema layer — the same positive whitelist + forbidden-token deny clause that descriptors[*].value uses. Canonical-set-membership invariant: every 'allowed_values' array carries minItems == maxItems == N AND uniqueItems == true AND items.enum of length N, where N is the canonical count (5 for rendering_style / palette_family / image_role / layout_pattern, 4 for modifier). With N unique items drawn from an N-element enum, the only valid array is a permutation of the canonical set — a tampered file that ships `["flat_vector"] * 5` would fail uniqueItems, and a file that omits a value would fail minItems; neither false-greens. Defense in depth: the runtime image-request gate (when wired) MUST cross-check every dimension value against the matching 'allowed_values' AND independently re-apply the deny pattern. This taxonomy is intentionally minimal — five dimensions × ≤5 values — and is not a mirror of any external image-style catalog. Adding, removing, or modifying a dimension or value is a paired schema / template / validator-probe change.

id.description: Synthetic request identifier. Same lowercase-identifier positive whitelist + forbidden-token deny clause as descriptors[*].value; never a real customer / product / project name.

modifier.description: Optional. When omitted, the runtime gate (when wired) applies no modifier. When present, MUST be one of the closed enumeration values.

synthetic_requests.description: Optional synthetic composed-request list. Each item demonstrates a fully composed image request whose four required dimensions (and optional modifier) all draw from image_taxonomy.<dim>.allowed_values. Length is bounded so a tampered file cannot smuggle a large free-form payload here. The schema's per-dimension enum lock means a tampered request cannot use a value outside the canonical taxonomy. Empty array is acceptable — this list is a documentation aid, not a contract requirement.
